examples.en: My older sister studied nursing at a junior college.

examples.ko: 전문대는 보통 이 년이나 삼 년 만에 졸업해요.
examples.en: You usually graduate from a junior college in two or three years.
I graduated from junior college and went straight into a company.
There is one junior college in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 전문대 입학 시험을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger brother is preparing for a junior college entrance exam.

examples.ko: 전문대와 대학교 중에서 어디로 갈지 고민이에요.
examples.en: I'm torn between a junior college and a university.

explain: 4년제 '대학교'와 짝으로 자주 말하고, 보통 과정이 더 짧고 직업 기술을 배우는 쪽이에요. 정식 이름은 '전문대학'이지만 말할 때는 대부분 '전문대'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I learned cooking at a junior college.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전문대'의 정식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the formal name for '전문대'.

phrases.en: I graduated from a junior college and got a job right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교를 마쳤다고 말할 때 '졸업하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '졸업하다' to say you finished school.
phrases.en_equiv: to graduate from a junior college

phrases.en: My younger sibling attends a junior college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 학교에 다니고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone is currently enrolled.

explain_en: It is often paired with the four-year '대학교', and its programs are usually shorter and focused on job skills. The formal name is '전문대학', but in speech people mostly say '전문대'.

examples.en: Our school's student council is preparing the festival.

examples.ko: 학생회는 한 달에 한 번 회의를 해요.
examples.en: The student council has a meeting once a month.
My friend is leading the student council this year.
I will join the student council next year too.
A new president of the student council was elected.
The student council and the teachers discussed it together.

explain: 중고등학교에서는 '학생회', 대학교에서는 '총학생회'를 많이 써요. 반 안의 일은 '반장'이 맡고, 학교 전체를 대표하는 사람은 '학생회장'이에요.

phrases.en: Our school's student council president is a third-year student.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 전체를 대표하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who represents the whole school.

phrases.en: The student council meeting is at lunchtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생회 사람들이 모여 하는 회의예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A meeting held by the student council members.

phrases.en: Our university's student union is holding an event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교 전체의 학생회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The student council of a whole university.

explain_en: Middle and high schools say '학생회', and universities often say '총학생회'. Matters inside a class are handled by the '반장' (class president), while the head of the whole school is the '학생회장'.

examples.en: Children's powder medicine is mixed with water and taken.
If the powder medicine is bitter, I mix it with syrup.

examples.ko: 이 약은 알약 말고 가루약으로 주세요.
examples.en: Please give me this medicine as powder, not as pills.

examples.ko: 가루약을 먹을 때는 사레들리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to choke when you take powder medicine.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸려서 병원에서 가루약을 받아 왔어요.
examples.en: I caught a cold and got powder medicine at the hospital.

examples.ko: 가루약이 입안에 남아서 물을 한 컵 더 마셨어요.
examples.en: The powder stayed in my mouth, so I drank another cup of water.

explain: 병원이나 약국에서 '가루약으로 주세요'처럼 약의 모양을 고를 때 써요. '알약', '물약', '시럽'과 짝으로 같이 나와요. 아이들 약은 가루약으로 받는 경우가 있어요.

phrases.en: I take powder medicine with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가루약과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요. 약은 '먹다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb with 가루약. Use 먹다 for taking medicine.

phrases.en: Please give it to the child as a powder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 약국에서 약의 모양을 고를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for choosing the form of medicine at a hospital or pharmacy.

phrases.en: I tear open the powder packet and mix it with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가루약이 들어 있는 작은 종이 봉지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the small paper packet that holds the powder medicine.

explain_en: You use it at the hospital or pharmacy to choose the form of medicine, as in '가루약으로 주세요'. It comes as a set with '알약' (pill), '물약' (liquid medicine) and '시럽' (syrup). Children's medicine is sometimes given as powder.

en: to nurse; to tend; to attend

examples.en: The mother takes care of her sick child all night.
I took care of my grandmother for three days.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 간호하느라 모임에 못 갔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go to the gathering because I was taking care of my sick friend.
Nursing patients is hard work.
I'm taking care of my father at the hospital.
Because you took care of me, I recovered quickly.

explain: 아픈 사람 곁에서 돌볼 때 쓰고, 병원에서 일하는 직업은 '간호사'예요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 돌볼 때 '병간호'라는 말도 많이 해요. 아이나 노인을 평소에 돌보는 일에는 '돌보다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 아버지를 한 달 동안 병간호했어요.
phrases.en: I took care of my sick father for a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이 아픈 사람 곁에서 돌볼 때 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when family members care for a sick person.
phrases.en_equiv: to care for a sick person

phrases.example: 언니가 감기에 걸린 저를 간호해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My older sister took care of me when I caught a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 다른 사람을 위해 돌볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 주다 means caring for someone as a kindness.

phrases.en: My friend works as a nurse at a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 환자를 돌보는 직업을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the profession of caring for patients in a hospital.

explain_en: Use it for caring for a sick person at their side; the hospital job is '간호사' (nurse). For family caring for a patient, people also say '병간호'. For everyday care of children or older people, use '돌보다'.

examples.en: I went to the science museum with the kids on the weekend.
The science museum is not far from my house.
I saw a robot exhibit at the science museum.
This science museum has free admission.
Our school is going on a field trip to the science museum.

examples.ko: 이 과학관에는 직접 만져 볼 수 있는 실험이 많아요.
examples.en: This science museum has many experiments you can touch yourself.

explain: '-관'은 보고 배우는 건물 이름 끝에 붙어요. 박물관, 미술관, 도서관도 같아요. '과학관에 가다', '과학관을 구경하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I watched a fun experiment at the science museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에서'를 붙여 과학관 안에서 한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-에서' lets you say what you did inside the science museum.

phrases.en: We looked around the science museum all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가다'보다 안을 둘러보는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This sounds more like looking around inside than just 'going'.
phrases.en_equiv: to look around the science museum

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the science museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is often used to say where to meet.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the science museum

explain_en: The ending '-관' attaches to the names of buildings where you look and learn, like '박물관', '미술관' and '도서관'. It is used in phrases like '과학관에 가다' and '과학관을 구경하다'.

examples.en: We did the high jump at the school sports day.
A high jump athlete really flies high.
His body caught the high jump bar.
I find the long jump easier than the high jump.
This year's high jump record is better than last year's.
I watched the high jump final on TV.

explain: 육상 경기 종목 이름이에요. 비슷한 종목으로 '멀리뛰기', 장대를 쓰는 '장대높이뛰기'가 있어요. 운동은 '높이뛰기를 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: We did the high jump in PE class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 종목은 '하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sports events go with the verb 하다.

phrases.example: 동생은 높이뛰기 선수가 되고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: My younger brother wants to become a high jump athlete.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 종목을 하는 사람을 말할 때 '선수'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 선수 to name the athlete in this event.

phrases.en: There is a high jump event this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회에서 하는 경기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the event held in a competition.

explain_en: It is the name of a track and field event. Similar events are '멀리뛰기' (long jump) and '장대높이뛰기' (pole vault). You say '높이뛰기를 하다' for doing it.

examples.en: On the weekend I went to the public bathhouse with my mom.
Every neighborhood has at least one public bathhouse.

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에서 때를 밀어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever scrubbed your skin at a public bathhouse?

examples.ko: 대중목욕탕에 처음 가면 조금 부끄러울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Going to a public bathhouse for the first time can feel a bit embarrassing.
In winter, a lot of people go to the public bathhouse.
This public bathhouse has a sauna too.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '목욕탕'이라고 줄여 말해요. 찜질방과는 달리 주로 씻고 탕에 몸을 담그는 곳이에요.

phrases.en: I go to the bathhouse every Saturday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대중목욕탕'을 줄인 말로 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 대중목욕탕 that people use more often in daily life.

phrases.en: After exercising, I washed up at the bathhouse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 몸을 씻는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for washing your body at that place.

phrases.en: The admission fee for the public bathhouse is eight thousand won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어갈 때 내는 돈을 말할 때 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it when talking about the entrance fee.

explain_en: In daily life people usually shorten it to '목욕탕'. Unlike a '찜질방', it is mainly a place for washing and soaking in the baths.

t90.ax: This public bathhouse has a sauna too.

examples.en: A few people arrived at the meeting room first.
Please just buy two or three apples.
I called a few times, but there was no answer.
If you rest for a few hours, you'll be fine.
There are a few eggs left in the fridge.
I moved a few months ago.

explain: '두세'와 비슷하게 대략 몇 개를 말할 때 써요. 관형사라서 '두서너 개', '두서너 명'처럼 뒤에 단위 말을 꼭 붙여요. 단독 명사로 쓰는 말은 '두서넛'이에요.

phrases.en: I ate a few tangerines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 수를 대략 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a rough count of things.

phrases.en: I called my friend a few times yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 횟수를 대략 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a rough number of times.

phrases.en: I bought two or three pieces of bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: '두서너 개'보다 짧고 말할 때 더 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 두서너 개 and easier to say.

explain_en: Like '두세', it gives a rough small number. It is a determiner, so it must be followed by a counter word, as in '두서너 개' and '두서너 명'. The form that works as a noun on its own is '두서넛'.

examples.en: It has been half a year since I started studying Korean.

examples.ko: 반년 전에 이 도시로 이사 왔어요.
examples.en: I moved to this city half a year ago.
That went on for half a year.
We promised to meet again in six months.
My friend came back to Korea after half a year.

examples.ko: 운동을 시작하고 반년이 지나니까 몸이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: Half a year after I started exercising, my body had changed.

explain: '반년'은 육 개월과 같은 말이에요. 한 단어라서 붙여 쓰고, '반년 만에', '반년 전'처럼 시간 표현과 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I exercised every day for half a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반년 내내 이어진 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that continued for six months.

phrases.en: I went to my hometown for the first time in six months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜만에 다시 했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing something again after six months.

phrases.example: 한국에 온 지 육 개월이 됐어요.
phrases.en: It has been six months since I came to Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반년과 같은 뜻인데 숫자로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 반년, said with a number.

explain_en: 반년 equals 육 개월. It is written as one word, and it pairs with time expressions: 반년 만에 (after half a year), 반년 전 (half a year ago).

en: to be put on the market; to be released

examples.en: The new album comes out tomorrow.
That game was released last year.
The new product is due to be released soon.
It sold out as soon as it was released.

examples.ko: 발매된 지 십 년이 넘은 음반이에요.
examples.en: It's a record that has been out for over ten years.
It hasn't been released in Korea yet.

explain: '발매되다'는 음반, 게임, 책, 물건이 처음 팔기 시작할 때 써요. 음악에서는 '출시'보다 '발매'를 더 많이 써요. 영화는 '개봉되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When is the album release date?
phrases.nuance_ko: 음반, 게임, 책이 팔리기 시작하는 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day an album, game or book goes on sale.

phrases.example: 새 게임은 다음 달 발매 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new game is scheduled for release next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 나올 계획이라는 뜻으로 공지에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is planned to be released; common in announcements.

phrases.en: The company is releasing a new book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the seller or company is the subject.

explain_en: 발매되다 is used when a record, game, book or product goes on sale for the first time. For music, 발매 is used more often than 출시. For movies, use 개봉되다.

examples.en: When I'm tired, I make sure to take a vitamin supplement.
Swallow this vitamin tablet with water.
I bought a vitamin supplement for my child at the pharmacy.

examples.ko: 비타민제 한 알을 물과 함께 먹어요.
examples.en: I take one vitamin pill with water.

examples.ko: 비타민제도 먹고 있는데 왜 이렇게 피곤할까요?
examples.en: I'm even taking vitamins, so why am I so tired?

examples.ko: 비타민제만 먹지 말고 과일도 많이 드세요.
examples.en: Don't just take vitamins; eat plenty of fruit too.

explain: '비타민'은 영양소 자체를 말하고, '비타민제'는 알약이나 젤리처럼 먹는 제품을 말해요. 일상에서는 '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'라고도 해요. 더 넓게 건강을 위해 먹는 것은 '영양제'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I take my vitamins every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '비타민제' 대신 '비타민'이라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk people often say 비타민 instead of 비타민제.

phrases.en: I bought supplements for my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비타민뿐 아니라 건강을 위해 먹는 것을 모두 말해서 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word covering any supplement taken for health, not just vitamins.

phrases.en: I take a vitamin supplement after meals.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비타민제'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb phrase paired with 비타민제.

explain_en: '비타민' is the nutrient itself, while '비타민제' is the product you take, such as a pill or jelly. In daily talk people also say '비타민을 챙겨 먹다'. The broader word for health supplements is '영양제'.

examples.ko: 수저통에서 숟가락 두 개만 꺼내 주세요.
examples.en: Please take just two spoons out of the utensil holder.
There is a utensil holder on every table in the restaurant.
The utensil holder is empty, so please fill it quickly.
I washed the utensil holder clean and left it to dry.

examples.ko: 이사 가서 새 수저통을 하나 샀어요.
examples.en: After moving, I bought a new utensil holder.
The child spilled the chopsticks from the utensil holder.

explain: '수저'는 숟가락과 젓가락을 함께 부르는 말이라 수저통에는 둘 다 들어가요. 식당에서 수저를 직접 꺼내 쓰게 놓아 둔 통도 이렇게 불러요.

phrases.en: I opened the spoon holder and took out chopsticks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수저를 꺼낼 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for taking utensils out of the holder.

phrases.en: After washing dishes, I put the utensils in the holder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수저를 정리해서 보관할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting utensils away.
phrases.en_equiv: to put utensils in the holder

phrases.en: Please put a spoon holder on every table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 수저통을 준비할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when setting up holders in a restaurant.

explain_en: '수저' refers to a spoon and chopsticks together, so both go into a 수저통. At restaurants, the container left on the table for self-service utensils is also called this.

examples.en: Yukhoe is raw meat, so it has to be fresh.
At the restaurant I ordered yukhoe and bibimbap.

examples.ko: 육회에 배와 계란 노른자를 올려 먹어요.
examples.en: We eat yukhoe topped with pear and egg yolk.

examples.ko: 저는 육회를 처음 먹어 봤는데 맛있었어요.
examples.en: It was my first time eating yukhoe and it was tasty.
I was worried whether I would like yukhoe, but it was fine.
I like yukhoe and raw fish too.

explain: '육'은 고기, '회'는 익히지 않은 음식을 부르는 글자예요. 보통 소고기를 양념해서 먹어요. 생선을 날것으로 먹는 음식은 '생선회'예요. '회' 앞에 오는 재료만 달라요.

phrases.en: I tried yukhoe for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '육회'와 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with yukhoe.

phrases.en: I had yukhoe bibimbap for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥 위에 육회를 올린 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a dish with yukhoe on top of rice.

phrases.example: 저는 날고기를 싫어해서 육회를 못 먹어요.
phrases.en: I don't like raw meat, so I can't eat yukhoe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 육회를 먹을 수 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you can't eat yukhoe.

explain_en: '육' means meat and '회' is food eaten uncooked. It is usually seasoned beef. Raw fish is called '생선회', so the ingredient before '회' changes.
